newsitem.title: HUNGARY: LIRA AGENCY CROSS HIGHLIGHTS BCE FUTURES TRADING.
newsitem.headline: LIRA AGENCY CROSS HIGHLIGHTS BCE FUTURES TRADING.

text.p: One major deal at steady price in Italian lira futures highlighted slow trading on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on Friday, dealers said.
The deal, an agency cross, was made at an unchanged 117 forint price for 6,077 lots, which gave the bulk of the day's total 8,908 lots or 1.178 billion forint turnover.

Dealers said investors took a wait-and-see attitude after substantial amounts of funds were drained off the market in the past two or three months and waiting for fresh incentives on the meeting of the G7 meeting, starting on Friday in U.S.
"Nobody knows what will happen there, but everybody has some ideas and wishes these ideas to become true," said Janos Szojka of Swap brokerage.
"These hopes do not necessarily coincide as there are ones who want a stronger dollar, while others want a weaker dollar."
"There are some who hope the yen will weaken while others believe that a stronger yen will be necessary to change a (Japanese) surplus (with the US) in foreign trade," Szojka said.
On Friday, dollar futures fell for two maturities, by 0.4 forints to 191.60 for September and by 0.6 forints to 197.70 for December, while mark futures were mixed.

On the Budapest Stock Exchange's currency futures section mark futures edged up for December 1997 and December 1998 by 0.21 forints and 0.16 forints to 116.08 and 130 forints, respectively, while December dollar gave up 1.14 forints to end at 197.45.
